PAUL, Minn., April 08, 2026**--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Second sentence of the paragraph under the "Energy" subtitle should read: "Energy reported a pretax loss of $133.6 million for the second quarter of fiscal year 2026, which represents a $54.2 million decrease versus the prior year period" (instead of "Energy reported a pretax loss of $133.6 million for the first quarter of fiscal year 2026, which represents a $54.2 million decrease versus the prior year period"). The company reported a net loss of $147.1 million and revenues of $8.4 billion for the quarter that ended February 28, 2026, compared to a net loss of $75.8 million and revenues of $7.8 billion in the second quarter of fiscal year 2025. Energy reported a pretax loss of $133.6 million for the second quarter of fiscal year 2026, which represents a $54.2 million decrease versus the prior year period.

**CHS Inc.** reported a second quarter fiscal 2026 net loss of **$147.1 million** on revenues of **$8.4 billion**, compared with a net loss of $75.8 million and revenues of $7.8 billion a year earlier, reflecting wider losses despite higher sales. The energy segment posted a pretax loss of **$133.6 million**, a larger loss than the prior year period, driven by significantly higher renewable energy credit expenses and hedging losses, partly offset by better crack spreads and refined fuels mix. Grains recorded a pretax loss of $17.9 million and agronomy a pretax loss of $11.5 million, both slightly worse than the prior year, as weaker oilseed crush and crop nutrient margins outweighed benefits from corn exports and the CF Nitrogen joint venture. For the first six months of fiscal 2026, CHS reported income before income taxes of $107.2 million and net income attributable to CHS Inc. of $113.4 million, both below the prior year’s six-month results.

# CHS earnings down in second quarter. INVER GROVE HEIGHTS, MINNESOTA, US — CHS Inc. posted a loss of $147.1 million and revenues of $8.4 billion for the second quarter of fiscal 2026, squeezed by headwinds in its grain segment, including weaker crush margins, and higher expenses for its energy segment. Results for the three months ended Feb. 28 compared with a loss of $75.8 million and revenues of $7.8 billion during the same period in fiscal 2025, CHS said in its April 8 report. The grains segment — primarily corn, oilseeds, wheat and specialty grains product lines — posted a second-quarter pretax loss of $17.9 million, which compared with a loss of $8.4 million a year ago. Corporate services swung to a pretax loss of $1.9 million in the second quarter after posting a profit of $14.5 million a year ago. ## Ardent Mills earnings down in second quarter. ## CHS earnings decline in second quarter. # Popular Articles.
